common_name: Pink Drift Rose (Low-Growing Bright Pink Groundcover Rose)

planting.note: Plant container roses in late winter through spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Pink Drift requires at least 6 hours of direct sun daily for the best flowering.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Pink Drift is a bright rose-pink member of the Drift series of groundcover roses developed by Meilland International, combining the low, spreading habit and disease resistance of groundcover roses with the repeat-blooming density of modern landscape roses. It stays low, under 18 inches, forming a wide, dense mat of semi-double pink flowers from spring through hard frost, with spent blooms dropping cleanly on their own so no deadheading is needed. Its excellent black spot and powdery mildew resistance makes it especially reliable through humid Gulf South summers when unresistant roses struggle. Use it for edging, slope erosion control, or mass plantings; shear lightly in late winter to keep growth dense and vigorous.

common_name: White Drift Rose (Low-Growing White Groundcover Rose)

planting.note: Plant container roses in late winter through spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; White Drift requires at least 6 hours of direct sun daily for the best flowering.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; White Drift is a pure white-flowered member of the Drift series of groundcover roses developed by Meilland International, combining the low, spreading habit and strong disease resistance of groundcover roses with the repeat-blooming density of modern landscape roses. It stays low, under 18 inches, forming a wide, dense mat of double white flowers from spring through hard frost, with spent blooms dropping cleanly on their own so no deadheading is needed. Its clean white color works well as a unifying element in a mixed rose bed or as a bright edging along a walk. Excellent black spot and powdery mildew resistance make it especially reliable through humid Gulf South summers; shear lightly in late winter to keep growth dense.

common_name: Apricot Drift Rose (Low-Growing Apricot-Orange Groundcover Rose)

planting.note: Plant container roses in late winter through spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Apricot Drift requires at least 6 hours of direct sun daily for the best flowering.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Apricot Drift bears warm apricot-orange, semi-double flowers on the same low, dense, spreading Drift-series habit developed by Meilland International, combining the coverage and toughness of groundcover roses with the repeat bloom of modern landscape roses. It stays low, under 18 inches, forming a wide mat of color from spring through hard frost, with spent blooms dropping cleanly on their own so no deadheading is needed. Its warm color pairs nicely with the cooler pinks and reds of other Drift series members in a mixed mass planting. Excellent disease resistance makes it especially reliable through humid Gulf South summers; shear lightly in late winter to keep growth dense.

common_name: Icy Drift Rose (Low-Growing Icy White-Pink Groundcover Rose)

planting.note: Plant container roses in late winter through spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Icy Drift requires at least 6 hours of direct sun daily for the best flowering.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Icy Drift bears double flowers that open blush pink and fade to a cool near-white as they age, giving a soft, icy two-tone effect on the same low, dense, spreading Drift-series habit developed by Meilland International. It stays low, under 18 inches, forming a wide mat of color from spring through hard frost, with spent blooms dropping cleanly on their own so no deadheading is needed. Its gentle, cool coloring works well in pastel plantings or as a softening edge along a walk or border. Excellent disease resistance makes it especially reliable through humid Gulf South summers; shear lightly in late winter to keep growth dense and vigorous.
